narrative.weekly_mirror: When Rojas offered to recommend you for the department head role, you read her email three times and closed your laptop, caught between the chance to shape curriculum for hundreds of students and the children who already rely on you. Earlier, you spent two hours helping families with their essays, including offering individual support; Diego’s pride mattered too: "First time he's gotten above a C on a written assignment."
narrative.tension_explanation: The choice feels difficult because both kinds of impact are real to you: changing an unfair system and protecting the trust you have built with the students and families in front of you. It makes sense that a salary or a logistical solution does not settle the deeper question of who will be there for those children.
narrative.reflective_question: When you picture the department head role alongside Diego and the Tuesday-and-Thursday students, what feels hardest to let go of?

grounded_quotes: First time he's gotten above a C on a written assignment.

With active Drift, describe the repeated choices plainly, without a verdict about the person.
Keep the language easy to say aloud. Avoid abstract phrases such as "a quiet contrast", "what does the contrast bring up", "this action from the week", and repeated "these moments sit alongside" constructions. Name the people, choices, or circumstances you mean.
